operations.comment: ; 16-byte iNES header: NES signature, 16 PRG units, 16 CHR units, mapper 4, horizontal initial mirroring, no trainer. Hardware metadata, not executable CPU bytes.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $8020.
; Set rendering and MMC3 RAM/mirroring state, choose CHR registers, clear work RAM and enter the staged screen sequence. The caller supplies A for the initial PPU writes.
; Transition entry skips initial PPU/MMC3 setup, blanks display and resets CHR/palette/work state before staged scene selection.

; Initialize the two movement parameter defaults, then optionally run the stage selector. Ordinary startup selects stage zero and resets the player variant, bonus-unit counter, health/capacity and spare lives.
; Wait two frames before the optional control-flag transition and common scene load. This entry is also used after stage changes and checkpoint recovery.
; Control flag bit 0 requests the pair04 transition helper before loading the stage.

; Blank the display and reset scene buffers while preserving checkpoint mode. Start stage audio only outside the timed player mode, then load stage, variant and common palettes. Fresh starts clear the $013C work area; checkpoint or special mode retains it before the fixed-bank continuation.

; The first entry delays and returns to the title transition with stage zero. The second runs the pair12 selection screen while saving stage_index; a zero result remaps the old stage, resets player defaults and reenters the stage loader. Other results reset the transition stack.
; Wait64frames, disable split/rendering and save current stage around option screen. Nonzero selection restarts transition; zero remaps stage and restores player defaults before stage load.

; Save the current stage and camera/map coordinates before selecting one of four alternate stages. Except for selector 3, also snapshot player timers, variant and movement defaults, then clear them for the alternate scene. The saved fields support the checkpoint restoration path below.
; Clear special player/shake state and the $011C work area, recover the remembered mode byte and mark checkpoint restoration active before reloading the selected stage.
; Clear split rendering, flashing and overlays, then blank display and audio state. Stage $30 advances to $35; other stages increment normally before common loading.
; Special successor for stage $30: select stage $35 and reenter the stage loader.
; Advance stage_index and reenter the common stage loader.

; Initialize the stage-selection display, clear vertical scrolling and choose CHR/palette resources. Queue the six-tile heading, then the twelve-tile stage name. The name-only entry uses a stage-indexed little-endian pointer table in this PRG pair.
; Queue twelve stage-name tiles selected by the stage-indexed source pointer table at PPU $218E.

; Poll once per frame. Directional presses select stages 0..$3A with wraparound; Start returns to the caller. Select enters a sound selector over IDs 0..$3B. Its two repeat timers delay held A/B changes by ten frames initially, then four frames; Up requests the selected sound while preserving X.
; Select a sound ID with bounded wraparound and independent held-button repeat delays; Select returns to stage selection.
; Queue the two tile codes for sound ID X at PPU $2210. The ID table remains local to PRG pair0/1.

; Sound-selector display bytes: the queue entry reads two tile codes per sound ID using $881C + 2*X, with X bounded to 0..$3B. The final eight bytes lie beyond that lookup span; their role remains uncertain.

; Install movement script $893B and state $44 on the current object, replace the remembered companion, and construct slot 3 with type $75/state $0B. This scripted scene uses its own CHR register, palette, animation and fixed coordinates; preserve the caller's object slot.

; Pace sound $17 while polling the departure movement script. When the signed X position passes the left-side threshold, switch to state $45/script $8A04 and change the remembered companion animation and slot3 state.

; Several state-table entries share this block. They poll movement and pace sound, wait for countdowns, shake the screen, and replace the remembered companion at scripted points. Leaving the signed coordinate bounds or completing the last delay resets the stack into the alternate scene; the exact story event remains uncertain.
; Count down the scripted departure delay, then reset the stack into the alternate scene.

; Clear the player slot and run stage/object initialization, then enable rendering unless collision flags bit3 suppresses it. Checkpoint mode restores saved position and equipment; special mode and ordinary starts select separate initialization paths.

; Restore the saved player coordinates and remembered palette/mode. If the current mode timer is zero, recover the saved movement limits, variant and secondary timer; a nonzero saved low timer becomes a short two-tick mode interval. Reset flashing and checkpoint flags, then enter ordinary player initialization. The adjacent special-mode entry uses a separate spawn helper except on stage $34.
; Stages $35 and $36 have dedicated spawn helpers; remaining stages use collision flags and remembered mode to choose the player initializer.
; Run the stage $35 spawn helper and join frame-state initialization.
; Run the stage $36 spawn helper and join frame-state initialization. The normal-spawn entry clears the remembered mode/palette and tests stage flags for facing and palette overrides.
; Stage collision flag bit5 sets the player animation facing bit.
; Stage collision flag bit1 selects the special remembered palette/mode setup.
; Use palette $27, or $28 on stage4, and remember it for player restoration. Mark the associated mode active with $FF.
; Stage collision flag bit7 selects a separate player spawn initializer.
; Run the bit7 spawn handler and join common frame-state initialization.
; Choose ordinary player reset when the remembered mode is zero; otherwise initialize that mode and its banked support.
; Initialize the remembered player mode and pair04 support before joining frame-state initialization.

; The first entry performs ordinary player reset. The shared continuation clears parity and rectangle selection, skips pair04 setup on five special stages, and chooses an alternating demo script before the frame loop.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $8C76.
; Yield one frame, allow scripted input, and derive newly pressed player buttons as current AND NOT previous. Pause/title exits precede player-state dispatch.

; Honor Start pause only when the pair02 status is nonnegative and its result permits it. The pause helper renders with player OAM reserved. Otherwise consume the deferred spawn request before normal state dispatch.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $8CCF.
; Reserve player OAM space, alternate the per-frame parity byte, clear extra motion, and push the dispatch return address. Stage-specific Y tests precede the state handler.
; Join state-table dispatch after the stage-specific position test.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $8D21.

; Handle the low-Y special case, then fetch a little-endian handler from the player state table. X identifies the player object; the handler RTS returns through the explicitly stacked frame continuation.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $8D41.
; Outside the signed special scene mode, thirty bonus units award one spare life and sound $26; the following entry retains any excess units.
; Consume thirty units from the threshold counter after its reward/sound event, retaining any excess for later frames.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $8D5E.

; Apply camera tracking and collision helpers, render several OAM partitions with separate cursors, then update objects and timers. The 16-bit countdown triggers the fixed-bank transition helper at zero.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $8F02.
; Follow the player only on permitted axes and directions. Distance from screen center $80 becomes a signed step clamped to -4..4; pin the player coordinate to the center after tracking.

; Reset vertical motion, movement timing and animation, then choose the speed limit from the scene default or contact bit1 override. Zero health enters the death handler; the remembered mode may force limit3, zero speed and its saved palette.
; Contact bit1 overrides the ordinary player speed limit with three.
; Install Y as the player speed limit, clear material-C contact and test health before restoring any remembered terrain mode.
; Zero health transfers to the death-sequence initializer.
; Return directly unless the remembered player mode needs its speed/palette override.
; The remembered mode fixes speed limit3, stops horizontal motion and reloads its palette only when selection differs.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $9015.

; Probe the current tile, handle stage and mode exceptions, then choose player behavior from timers, parity and status fields. Exits select stage transitions, mode changes and material-specific player handlers.
; Save the pair02 material response before testing remembered mode. Negative responses or value3 enter the special material handler only when that mode is inactive.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $909F.
; Dispatch newly pressed action bits first, then held directional bits. Left/right update the animation flip flag before entering shared acceleration.
; Choose direction mask2 before the common acceleration entry.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $90E8.
; Save the old direction, install the new direction and test reversal. Increase speed toward the per-object limit and clamp the special limit-six case to a minimum speed of four.
; Use the increased speed as a timing-table index, reload horizontal movement parameters and join the animation reset path.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $912C.
; Load the movement countdown and reset animation to zero if necessary before common collision and interaction processing.
; Reload sprite animation data after resetting the movement animation index.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $913E.
; One entry joins common movement processing; the following action entry passes $18 to a banked helper before searching for a type-$0F interaction.

; Search nonplayer slots1..5 for type $0F, run its interaction probes and transfer to its player interaction handler when accepted. If no usable target exists, restore player slot0 and choose remembered-mode movement or ordinary idle/coasting.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $917F.
; Contact flags select deceleration. Otherwise compare speed against its limit and choose idle/coasting behavior; the special mode $0D shares the limit path.
; Clear direction, speeds and movement timing. Select animation $16 only when it changes, then enter common collision/interaction handling.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $91C6.
; Wait for the movement countdown, then reduce a nonzero speed by one. Zero speed joins idle reset; remaining speed reloads its timing row.
; A remaining nonzero speed reloads movement timing; reaching zero joins the idle reset.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $91D8.
; Continue the shared idle movement path; no additional state changes occur here.
; Use the reduced speed to select the ordinary timing row, then reload horizontal movement parameters before common movement.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $91E2.
; The first entry joins common movement. The next entry probes a point two pixels below the player and saves the material result for movement decisions.
; Probe a point two pixels below the player and remember the returned material.
; Clear object status bit2, which distinguishes coasting/contact movement in the player speed logic.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $9203.
; Set bit 2 of the object status field. Later handling of this flag is outside this fragment.

; Material $0D uses animation $17 and the third seven-byte timing row. Ordinary contact uses the second row; the internal speed-index entry adds seven before loading object_movement_countdown. Exact delay units follow the per-frame countdown consumer.

; Three seven-byte player movement-delay rows. The ordinary index adds seven to speed; material $0D adds fourteen and selects animation $17. Per-object countdown consumers pace subsequent speed steps.
; Add seven to the speed index and load the acceleration countdown from the second seven-byte table row.
; Two seven-byte acceleration-delay rows; the visible consumer selects row two by adding seven to the speed index.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $9260.
; Run collision response, pace the movement sound, select object interactions and material-specific handlers, and advance animation when moving. Direction reversal may reset movement timing.
; Compare speed and direction against previous direction, resetting timing when required.
; Return $FF after a direction reversal at or above the speed limit; callers use the negative flag to begin the reversal state.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $92E8.
; Return zero from the preceding movement test; the following entry starts player state one. These are distinct entry paths.

; Stop horizontal movement, select animation $17 and flip facing. The following handlers poll that animation or run a short material-$0D movement state; completion returns to ordinary movement, while loss of vertical contact enters the airborne path.
; Poll the reversal animation until its completion flag, allowing the action button to restart vertical movement.
; Wait for reversal animation completion, allowing the primary action to restart movement.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $937B.
; Clear both vertical direction bits while retaining horizontal direction and unrelated flags.

; Start player state2 with animation $22 and movement script $942D. Choose scene motion/speed defaults, or the contact override, and clear vertical motion and action timing. Initial horizontal speed controls status bit3; facing selects script flag bits. The remembered mode transfers to its own initializer.

; Update held-button script release, object and terrain collisions, horizontal steering and side blocking. Script completion enters the remembered-mode falling path. Vertical contact chooses object/terrain landing handlers; special materials and banked probes may override the state. Internal setup entries install scripts $95C6/$944A or remembered-mode $95D8, animation frame4/5 and status bit5 before clearing vertical motion and direction bit2.
; Only while direction bit3 is set, probe the offset point (+12,-20). Return negative and remember material3 when accepted; all other results return zero.
; Remember collision material3 and return $FF so the caller enters the special-contact state.
; Return zero when the upper-point material3 probe does not match.

; Status bit5 prevents repeated script changes. Releasing action bit0 after ten ticks, or holding it until the configured motion threshold, installs the ordinary or remembered-mode release script. Clear script control bits $60 and reset movement counters to let decoding resume.

; Read held left/right buttons to accelerate in the current direction or decelerate before reversal. work_00 carries the facing bit; Y carries the desired direction mask. With no direction pressed, return without changing speed.
; Moving opposite the requested right direction enters timed braking before reversing.
; Request right direction mask1 and clear the sprite facing bit before common air acceleration.
; Request left direction mask2 and facing bit2. Existing rightward speed must pass the braking path before leftward acceleration.

; Unless status bit4 indicates braking, a nonzero steering timer delays the next speed step. When ready, install facing and clear braking, saving the desired direction while choosing a speed-indexed delay row.
; State $11 uses the second eight-byte acceleration delay row.
; Reload the steering delay, preserve vertical direction bits and install the requested horizontal mask. Increase speed only below the current limit plus one, then reload movement parameters.

; Use status bit4 and the steering timer to pace braking. Set facing, reload a speed-indexed delay and reduce speed by one before updating horizontal movement parameters. The next steering frame can choose the opposite direction once speed reaches zero.
; Return from the shared air steering/acceleration/braking paths.
; Air steering delays: two eight-byte acceleration rows at $976F/$9777 (state $11 chooses the second), followed by an eight-byte braking row at $977F. Speed indexes the selected row.
; Skip side probes at zero horizontal speed. Direction bit0 selects right-side probes; bit1 selects left-side probes.
; Test the left side through pair02 geometry helpers and the fixed-bank point probe. A hit joins the shared speed-stop path, with remembered-mode material2 handling first.
; Test the right side through pair02 geometry helpers, then the horizontal point list before deciding whether to stop motion.
; The pair02 side probe hit enters the common stop-and-mark-blocked path.
; No helper hit: test the horizontal point list. A zero result leaves horizontal movement unchanged.

; Remembered mode may invoke material2 handling before a blocked side stops speed. If health is zero, enter the death sequence; otherwise clear horizontal speed and steering delay and set status bit3.
; Return after side collision processing or a clear side probe.

; Start state3, animation $1A and direction bit3 with a table-timed vertical motion step. Clear contact bit1 and steering delay. Remembered mode uses script $9873; special scene mode also increments its bounded progress counter when the player is far enough right.

; Advance state3 through contact-triggered animation and vertical-speed phases. Action bit1 can restart or mark the contact phase; remembered mode polls a script while ordinary movement advances through a delay table capped at motion index11. Steering and side probes precede object/terrain contact, special material and landing decisions. The final initialization entry stops motion in state$0B and derives shake/transition delays from a four-byte variant record.
; Two four-byte player-variant landing records: byte0 is shake duration, bytes2/3 are the little-endian transition countdown. Byte1 is skipped by this consumer; its role is unresolved.

; Update object contact and landing animation, restoring ordinary movement when animation bit0 completes. A separate special-stage entry selects state$4D, stops movement and waits twenty ticks before the scene transition helper.
; Count down twenty ticks before entering the locked-scroll scene wait.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $9AB3.
; Request sound three and initialize the falling state, or its remembered-mode alternative.
; The falling entry uses a separate remembered-mode script when that mode is active; ordinary mode initializes the gravity-like vertical sequence below.
; Transfer to the remembered-mode falling initializer.

; Install vertical motion7 (or4 for the alternate internal mode entry), direction bit3, animation5 and state4. Reset steering/material contact. The following state handler checks banked contact before terrain and advances the vertical-speed timer.
; Falling state4 reuses terrain/object landing responses and advances vertical speed on its timer.
; A terrain-point hit transfers to the shared terrain landing response.
; Decrement the falling frame timer; expiry advances vertical motion toward the cap of13.
; Increase vertical motion below13, reload motion parameters and wait sixteen frames before the next step.
; A new action bit1 press restarts the vertical action; otherwise process object and special-material contact.
; Restart the state3 vertical action from the falling state.
; Delay object contact while motion_remaining is nonzero. Once clear, a banked object hit selects the shared object landing response.
; Transfer to the shared object landing response.
; Probe the special upper material3 contact before horizontal steering and remaining state checks.
; The upper material3 hit enters the state5 contact sequence.
; Apply horizontal steering and side blocking, then test the banked player transition condition.
; Transfer to the material/player transition selected by the banked probe.
; The pair02 contact probe may select a separate player state before this frame returns.
; Transfer to the separate banked-contact response.
; Return from the falling state update.

; Initialize state5/animation $0A, stop motion, seed a signed phase counter and request sound $0E. The update entry probes ahead and above according to facing, handles away/down/action presses, and alternates stationary and vertical phases with a signed countdown. Loss of the probed material or phase bounds starts a facing-directed scripted exit in state7. Probably a climbing/contact sequence; the exact terrain identity remains uncertain.
; Material3 contact update: probe relative to facing and alternate vertical phases while accepting exit inputs.

; The first entry rejoins the scripted-air contact probe. Other entries choose fast or normal downward motion in state6, allow action bit0 to return to stationary state5, and apply falling acceleration with banked/material checks. The last entry flips facing and starts a direction-specific state2 script after sound2.
; Material3 falling update: permit return to contact, then test support and timed vertical acceleration.
; Unclassified boundary: isolated $60 has no independently supported routine entry or return contract. Keep the exact bytes; no code or data role is claimed.
; Install the supplied animation and reload sprite data, then resume the scripted-air state2.

; Separate object and terrain landing entries request sound4 and clear action/contact state. Type-$0B objects have a special response; other hits share palette/mode/material tests. Ordinary landing selects state9/animation3 for four ticks and caps high horizontal speed. Material7 installs the first four-byte script/motion/speed record and enters its dedicated state.

; Material7 movement setup begins with a four-byte record: script pointer low/high, vertical-action hold threshold and horizontal speed limit. Remaining bytes include its adjacent movement script; exact command grouping is not asserted here.

; While waiting in state9, maintain collision response and test stage/transition exceptions. After the four-tick timer return to ordinary movement, with a new action press allowed to restart vertical movement early.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $9F7F.
; Stop horizontal movement, then initialize state $0A and its animation/contact update.

; Finish state$0A initialization by clearing vertical motion and script counters, choosing animation $18 and clearing coasting. The update entry probes contacts and material response: transitions and remembered mode can override, while ordinary completion returns to movement.
; State$0A checks material/object responses before resuming ordinary or special-terrain movement.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $9FF2.
; Preserve Y and initialize mode counters before calling the fixed-bank helper. Meaning of this transition is unresolved.

; Recover the contacting object slot from the stack and compare its 16-bit X with the player. Face and move away from that object, select the ordinary or special-terrain knockback script, clear script timing and enter state$0C/animation8 with sound9.

; Advance animation and the knockback script, then reuse the ordinary vertical-contact and side-blocking responses. Script completion chooses falling or special-terrain movement. The second entry begins environmental damage state$0D: set temporary status, clear motion, select animation2 and the matching terrain script, then seed action-age and steering timers.

; Check banked contacts, permit a delayed action restart while health remains, then poll the movement script and reuse air-contact processing. Separate collision entries create an effect at the player, choose state$0E/animation$1D and an ordinary/special-terrain script. One entry also handles the locked-scroll boundary before installing that state.
; Request sound7 before the upper-contact position/effect helper.
; Pass the player position shifted up32 pixels to the pair04 effect helper with selector0, then request sound5. The repeated Y load is preserved exactly.

; The first entry checks a banked contact before reusing scripted-air logic. A state$0F interaction entry compares the participating objects, selects direction/facing and animation$17, then moves at speed7 while a timer and collision probes permit. Type-$0B contact instead selects state$10 and follows the linked object's frame-indexed vertical offset until a zero table value releases it.
; Maintain directed interaction motion until the countdown, support or side probe stops it.
; Follow the linked actor using its variant/frame-dependent vertical offset; a zero offset releases contact.

; Two four-byte linked-object vertical-offset rows, chosen by object variant then frame. Nonzero offsets place the player above that object; zero releases contact and selects the following movement record.

; Release state$10 from its linked object, clear contact bit3 unless the linked variant is1, and choose a four-byte script/motion-limit/speed record. Initialize state$11, animation$1E and fresh movement timing. The internal record selector uses linked-object variant and contact bit3 to choose one of four records.

; Four four-byte linked-object movement records begin at $A507: script pointer low/high, action-hold limit and speed limit. Linked variant selects an eight-byte half; contact bit3 selects its second record. Movement scripts follow within this binary-backed region.
; For linked-object variant1, permit a five-tick action window to set contact bit3 and reload the movement record. Then reuse scripted-air contact and movement handling.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $A5E8.
; Request sound$0A once when health is exhausted. The timer high bit suppresses repeated requests while the death sequence initializes.
; Set the movement-sound timer high bit to suppress repeated death sound requests.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $A5F9.
; Begin the exhausted-health sequence: clear contact action, status countdown and vertical motion before resetting the variant and initializing its death state.

; Enter state$12/animation9, disable normal control with gameplay bit2 and move in the existing or facing-derived horizontal direction. Its update runs speed5 for up to64 ticks, testing contact and terrain. Then state$13 stops horizontal motion and waits for animation$1F to finish, adding falling motion if unsupported. State$14/animation$20 stops all movement and chooses a special-terrain script or ordinary palette$23 before the restart prompt.
; Move at speed5 until contact, terrain or the64-tick delay selects the death landing phase.
; Wait for landing animation completion; preserve motion only while unsupported.

; Update animation/contact in the restart state. Once animation completes, no spare lives returns to the scene sequence; Start otherwise consumes a spare life and begins revival, restoring health12 and state$17/animation$15. Revival completion clears the disabled-control flag and chooses normal/material movement. An unsupported death entry instead installs state$15 and ordinary/special-terrain falling scripts.
; Finish revival, restore normal control and select the material-appropriate movement path.

; Continue the death script while testing object/terrain support. Collision flags$40 enable special-terrain mode and palette; finding support stops movement and joins the death landing animation. Script completion joins the next death phase, otherwise check side blocking.
; Use palette$27 for special terrain, with palette$28 on stage4.
; Stage4 uses palette$28 instead of$27.
; Remember the selected special-terrain palette and load it through pair02.

; Probe the material, set contact bit6 except on material2, and choose horizontal facing/direction from material5. Start speed2, animation$21 and script$A937 in state$16, resetting steering and action-age timers.

; Before animation frame2, check transitions and advance the movement script; afterwards reuse scripted-air contact handling. The following independent entry temporarily switches to player slot0, enters state$18/animation$0C, stops movement and clears status before installing the secondary-mode interval and preserving the caller slot.
; Wait for entry animation completion, then begin the secondary-mode movement script.
; Install state$19/script$A9FC and animation$13 with fresh script timing; request sound$3B.

; While the mode script runs, advance animation. On completion choose variant-dependent protection/status intervals, reload the variant or remembered terrain palette and a two-byte secondary-mode duration. Restore stage audio outside the primary timed mode, then select material, terrain-mode or ordinary movement.
; Two little-endian secondary-mode duration words, indexed by (player_variant - 1)*2 after the mode script completes.
; Install state$1A and script$AAFC, shift the player down8 pixels, and mark special-terrain mode active. Load its stage-dependent palette and request sound$22.
; Poll the terrain-entry script. On completion initialize the terrain falling state; while active, check the facing side for a wall and stop horizontal speed when blocked.
; Use the fixed-bank left-side point probe; a hit clears horizontal speed before checking vertical support.
; Test vertical support after the terrain-entry side probe; a hit restores ordinary player movement.
; Reset banked player motion state and resume ordinary movement after support is found.
; Return from the terrain-entry update. The following initializer first checks support before choosing a terrain falling state.
; Support found at terrain-fall initialization resets motion and returns to ordinary player movement.
; Without vertical support, zero health enters the unsupported death script; a living player gets state$1C falling motion.
; Transfer to the unsupported death sequence when the terrain-fall initializer finds no health.
; Reuse falling setup, then choose vertical motion2 and state$1C. The adjacent state update first checks the banked transition condition.
; Terrain-fall state$1C checks action exits, support, material6 direction input and side blocking.
; The banked transition condition selects the damage/mode-change initializer.
; Action bit0 leaves the terrain-fall state through ordinary vertical-action setup.
; Join the entry that clears vertical direction and begins the primary action.
; Action bit1 selects the stopped-action state; otherwise continue support checks.
; Join stopped-action initialization from the terrain-fall state.
; Probe vertical terrain support; no hit proceeds to object and overhead-material checks.
; Reset motion on support, with a moving material$0D exception. Otherwise cap horizontal speed at3 before ordinary movement resumes.
; Without terrain support, an object hit also restores ordinary movement.
; An object supports the player; return to ordinary movement.
; Probe twenty pixels above the player for material6. Directional input on that material enters the freely directed terrain-movement state.
; Only held directional bits enter directed terrain motion on material6.
; Check side blocking and return from terrain falling.
; Stop existing motion and clear the contact-action field. Zero health enters the death sequence; otherwise select state$1B and animation$0D for directional terrain movement.
; At a particular animation phase, action input can leave this state. Otherwise action bit1 selects stopped motion, and absence of held directions returns to terrain falling.
; Join primary-action setup from directed terrain motion.
; Action bit1 chooses the stopped-action state before direction decoding.
; Join stopped-action initialization from directed terrain motion.
; Held directional bits select the motion-record lookup; no direction returns to terrain falling.
; Initialize terrain falling when no direction remains held.

; Use the directional high nibble to index a four-byte record: facing override, direction mask, horizontal speed and vertical motion. A negative facing byte preserves facing. Reload both motion parameters and advance animation before axis-specific collision checks.

; For direction bit2, probe the upper points and a point24 pixels above. Collision flags$40 permit this motion; other hits run material handling, stop vertical motion and enter death if health reaches zero.

; For nonzero vertical motion with direction bit3, test vertical support, then object contact. A terrain hit checks its material and health before deciding whether held horizontal input keeps this state.

; Remember the supporting material and apply its response. Health loss enters death; otherwise no held horizontal direction returns to ordinary movement, while held direction merely stops vertical motion.
; An object support hit restores ordinary movement; no hit proceeds to the banked transition check.
; Return to ordinary movement after the supporting object is detected.
; Test the banked transition condition before side collision processing.
; Enter the damage/mode-change initializer selected by the banked transition probe.
; Check side blocking and return from directed terrain movement.

; Sixteen four-byte directed-terrain movement records indexed by the held directional high nibble: facing override (negative preserves facing), direction mask, horizontal speed index and vertical-motion index. Invalid/combined directional masks retain whatever records the original table supplies.
; Probe32 pixels above slot X: flags bit6 returns zero; absence returns $FF. The previous note had these results reversed.
; Probe32 pixels above slot X. Return zero when collision flags bit6 is present, otherwise $FF; callers can use the negative result to detect departure from special terrain.
; Enter state$1D with speed limit3 and hold limit10, script$AD83 and animation$22. Facing controls script flag bits; reset movement, steering, contact and action age before the banked player helper.

; Reuse held-action script control, then check banked transitions and terrain/object contact. Script completion returns to terrain falling. Material2/10 and upper contact select their specific effects or scripts; finish with steering, action restart and side collision. The internal exit entry clears terrain mode, restores variant palette and installs state$1E/script$AE48.

; The first entry joins the ordinary scripted-air contact path. The second starts state$1F with vertical motion2, then its update checks side collision and animation completion before returning to terrain falling.
; Wait for the exit animation while checking side blocking; completion returns to terrain falling.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $AE88.
; Call the pair04 player reset/transition helper, then continue the stage-exit state setup.

; Select state$20 and move toward the stage-selected side at speed4. The starting X and stage choose its delay; some stages also select exit sound$39/$3A. The update checks side material$0E, paces animation and eventually enters state$21 or the special scene transition. A later entry starts state$22/script$9475; after48 ticks it queues rectangle changes, updates linked actors and patches collision bytes before reusing air/script movement.
; Check the exit-facing material, count down the stage delay and finish through the next exit state.
; After48 ticks, advance the PPU rectangle, update linked actors and patch local collision bytes.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $AFE2.
; A positive selector chooses a four-byte record containing source and destination words. Queue a 12-by-2 PPU rectangle in the current PRG bank; zero/negative selectors do nothing.

; After the selected tile rectangle, queue three attribute bytes at each of $23E2 and $23EA from local sources $B0F0/$B0F3. Advance the rectangle selector; after record5 set it negative to disable further updates.
; Physical PRG banks 0/1; CPU execution alias $B063.
